subject: Decision Making
title: The Ideal Team Size
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Ideal Team Size.

hook.text: Jeff Bezos has a two-pizza rule: if a team needs more than two pizzas, it is too big to make good decisions.

buildup.text: Research confirms small teams decide faster. Communication lines grow exponentially: ten people have 45 connections.

discovery.text: The sweet spot for decision-making teams is five to seven people. Enough diversity without communication overload.

twist.text: Large groups work for brainstorming and information gathering.

climax.text: Team size is a design choice, not an accident. Choosing the right number is itself one of the most important decisions.

punchline.text: Five to seven deciders. Any more and communication kills speed and quality.

quiz.question: Why do large teams make worse decisions?
options: Communication lines grow exponentially, creating overload and slowing decisions
